content: This is the discussion thread for the Mathlib phrasebook announcement. Please find the phrasebook online here. The repository for contributing your own entries is available here.
Thank you for the excellent initiative, I love it! I hope I'll find some time to contribute.
I think @Rémy Degenne's blog here is useful to be included in the phrase book
I intend to open a PR with content from that blog post some time in the next few weeks.

I just threw down another handful of suggestions.

My idea is that there is a lot of value in having a large number of very short articles. The idea is that other references can discuss at length but these articles just overcome the coefficient of static friction. I guess we'll see how things develop.

That looks like a very useful resource. Thanks!

The first occurrence of "distributivity" on this page should be "associativity".

The first occurrence of "distributivity" on this page should be "associativity".

Thanks for the suggestion, corrected!

Terence Tao had a phrasebook in the form of spreadsheets, and I think some entries could be useful in the Mathlib phrasebook. I've included some examples below.

Informal statement Lean 4 formalization
Let a : ℕ → ℝ be a sequence converging to a limit L (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) (h : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 L)) or (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) (h : Tendsto a atTop (nhds L)) or (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) (h : map a atTop ≤ 𝓝 L)
Let f : ℕ → ℝ be a sequence summing to S (f : ℕ → ℝ) (S : ℝ) (h : HasSum f S) or (f : ℕ → ℝ) (S : ℝ) (hsum : Summable f) (hS : ∑' n, f n = S)
The interval [a,b) Set.Ico a b
Certainly I have no objection to anyone migrating anything useful from that phrasebook (which I have abandoned maintaining) to this new resource!

I made some comments on Michael's Differential Geometry PR. I would be happy to do a more detailed review of the math as per @Anne Baanen's request

Do you have a suggestion for someone who can proofread the mathematical contents?

Although I'm sure there are others more qualified than myself who could contribute.
... but I'm also sure some of these more qualified people may have less time available than you do. Feel free to take a look!

(And note that my entry is intentionally not trying to explain how everything works. That would be a different entry, more suitable for MIL, which should also get written. I hope to find time for that, but that's a different story!)
We should definitely add all the idioms involving filters. They confuse a lot of people.
Is there a review queue or process to ask for a review? I want to add more group theory stuff that's not already in MIL and opened a small PR to start.

Martin Dvořák said:

We should definitely add all the idioms involving filters. They confuse a lot of people.

@Martin Dvořák please review my open PR providing a phrasebook entry for filters: mathlib-phrasebook#5, and flag any missing idioms!

Li Xuanji said:

Is there a review queue or process to ask for a review? I want to add more group theory stuff that's not already in MIL and opened a small PR to start.

I think @Anne Baanen is usually reviewing phrasebook PRs. In this case, I wonder if MIL should be extended instead. What do you think; would you like to make a PR to that repository instead?
(Aside: if the mathlib overview is missing some significant group theory items, feel free to make a PR adding to the list. The things you're adding are probably fine.)

I am a bit hesitant to PR substantive material to MIL because my sense (based on reading MIL and also its README, etc) is that MIL's list of topics is somewhat "curated" and MIL teaches formalization through those topics, and does not have a goal of comprehensive topic coverage (by any criteria of comprehensiveness). I can provide a more detailed explanation if desired, and if this is inaccurate I would love to be corrected.

This might be a Verso question, but can an Exists statement be displayed in a way that shows the type of the existential witness? Consider, in the phrasebook, the statement for Hahn Banach. Clicking on exists_extension_norm_eq at https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib-phrasebook/Topological-vector-spaces/Notable-results/#Mathlib-Phrasebook--Topological-vector-spaces--Notable-results doesn't show the type of g, which is really the critical power of the theorem.
Maybe you can use pp.funBinderTypes? You could set it just for theorems like this.
Could you link the phrasebook to https://leanprover-community.github.io/documentation.html#how-tos if it's not done already. So that we have all documentation referenced in one place.
Seems like a good idea to me. cc @Anne Baanen
Thanks for spotting this, I seem to have totally forgot! website#917
The four quadrant documentation is looking really nice.
Thank you! The design comes from Divio, but the implementation is all hand-written interactive SVG :)
I remember when I started I only had Kevin's Natural numbers game, the situation overall has improved trememdeously in the last two years, in all aspects.
You don't want to know what it was like when I started ;-)
